title: Costly signals
idea: Anyone can claim to be good. A signal is believable when it is costly to fake, so people trust proof that a weaker version of you could not produce.
apply: To be believed, show evidence that is hard to fake: a sample, a track record, a guarantee. When judging others, discount cheap talk.
remind: Cheap talk is ignored. Show proof.
who: Ken, a freelancer whose proposals sound like everyone else's.

msgs.x: I am reliable, detail oriented, and passionate.

scenes.nar: Ken, a freelancer, writes that he is reliable, detail oriented, and passionate. The client replies that everyone says that.
Words cost nothing, so they prove nothing. A client wants evidence that would be hard to fake.

items.x: A free sample page, done well
A fixed price and a refund promise

scenes.nar: Michael Spence showed that signals work when they are costly to fake. Ken offers a sample done well, two references, and a refund promise.
The client calls a reference, hears glowing words, and signs a pilot. Ken wins the job without cutting his price.
